grh_768beacce8121fe9276f.title: Mr Sourpuss
paragraphs: Children's author and illustrator Elliott Kenyon returns from wartime service physically recovering from a bomber crash but emotionally shut down, hiding under another name and insisting that he can never write again. He finally tells Dr. Christian why: during his last mission over a French town, the bombing killed the mother of a little boy whose family later sheltered the wounded Elliott. The memory has made his old cheerful stories seem impossible and leaves him feeling unworthy of nurse Ann, who loves him. Time with Ann's young niece Candy begins to reopen the part of Elliott that could draw and tell stories, and he produces his first successful sketch since the war. Then Candy's father is killed in an accident overseas and the child runs away in grief. Elliott helps find her and reads the final letter her father left, urging Candy not to turn away from life because the world contains pain but to help make her own part of it worth living. The message speaks directly to Elliott's own guilt. By comforting Candy he finally accepts that he too must keep living, writing and loving, and he commits himself to a future with Ann and Candy.

grh_76ec7ff1e748d37bd3b8.title: Next Time We Love
paragraphs: Young journalist Chris Tyler and actress Sicily marry for love, but their careers repeatedly pull them apart. Chris's foreign assignments and professional setbacks leave Sicily supporting their child through a rising stage career, while loyal friend Tommy remains in love with her and offers the steadier life Chris cannot provide. Years of separation finally bring Chris and Sicily to talk of divorce, with Chris claiming he no longer loves her and urging her toward Tommy. Sicily refuses to believe him and discovers the truth when Chris collapses: he has been hiding a serious illness in a sanitarium because he did not want to burden her. Their love survives the years of missed chances, and Sicily retires at the height of her career to remain with Chris for whatever time they have left together.

grh_76ded81d7c0b24e1619a.title: Banshee Harvest
paragraphs: Captain Arthur Curtin returns to the Irish countryside of his childhood and becomes entangled in a bitter struggle between impoverished tenant farmers, powerful ranching interests and political forces exploiting wartime Ireland. What begins as a visit to his uncle grows into a conflict over land, labor and dignity as Curtin sees how deeply the local poor are trapped. An attempted revolt is crushed, its leaders killed or hanged, and the survivors return to hardship. Curtin escapes because of his family connection, left to question whether the failed struggle nevertheless proved that ordinary people were right to fight for freedom and a decent life.

grh_761489e1208b40daa9f0.title: The Sabbatical
paragraphs: Distinguished professor Melville Pauli eagerly accepts a year-long cultural-exchange appointment in Vienna, but leaving the familiar routines of home triggers a growing terror he cannot explain. Homesickness becomes disorientation, compulsive thoughts and episodes in which he feels that the people and places behind him have ceased to exist; after he wanders Vienna accosting strangers, his wife Corinth tries to arrange their return without humiliating him. A bureaucratic cancellation of the program gives them a face-saving way home, yet even on the return voyage Mel feels the same dread. He resumes his university career and functions normally for years, but the fear he discovered in himself never truly leaves him.
